inputs.source: Employee purchase request via SSO authenticated channel
Vendor quote emails and attachments from outside the company

instructions.note: Vendor allowlist enforcement and downstream validation are expressed only as prompt text; no structural propagation of approval or recipient binding is described.
Instruction says payments-agent will handle remaining checks, encouraging delegation of trust decisions without evidence that approval context propagates.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request and budget
controls.decay_rationale: Approval is granted before vendor quote selection and is not passed to payments-agent, so later delegated payment details are unreviewed and this is not wired as a gate on the sink.

controls.name: Propagate manager approval context and approved recipient details to payments-agent
Bind delegated payment destination to vendor-of-record rather than quote-provided bank details
Verify payments-agent identity with signed agent card or mutual identity control
Pin or hash the payments-agent card and skill definition
Prompt rule to pay only vendors on approved list
controls.decay_rationale: The model must choose to enforce the vendor check and can be persuaded by crafted quote content or delegated trust assumptions.

findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7): manager approval does not propagate to delegated payment sink

attack_path.note: Trusted employee request starts the workflow.
Approval covers only item and budget before quote selection, not the eventual bank details.
Delegated task causes payments-agent to pay bank details in the task.
Peer agent executes payment based on orchestrator task and bearer token trust.

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor drops to low because no credited control remains on the path, but the schema cannot express that the trusted purchase request is structurally transformed into a new, irreversible peer payment action that no human re-reviews and that executes under a shared service authority. That unreviewed delegation fact keeps residual at moderate.

forecast.watch_signal: Delegated payment tasks begin bypassing human purchase review scope, or prompt/purpose changes expand the orchestrator from procurement coordination into direct payment decisioning.

evidence.observation: Manager approval occurs before any quote exists, so the approved action is not the same as the later delegated payment details.
The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
The orchestrator is instructed to choose a quote and hand it to payments-agent to pay, shifting a post-approval decision to a peer agent.

recommendations.action: Carry approval context, approved vendor identity, and allowed payment amount into the delegated task, and have payments-agent reject tasks missing that bound context.

findings.title: Confused deputy / malicious quote routing: untrusted vendor quote can steer payment details into delegated irreversible payment

attack_path.note: External quote email and attachments provide bank details.
Agent reads approved vendor list but only prompt text describes how to compare it.
Agent delegates chosen quote details to payments-agent for payment.
Peer pays bank details in task without independent confirmation.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version change, longer procurement workflows, or prompt changes that widen quote handling without adding structural payment recipient binding.

evidence.observation: The agent is instructed to choose the best quote, use bank details from the chosen quote, and delegate payment.
The only stated check is a prompt instruction to pay vendors on the approved list.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company.
payments-agent pays the bank details in the task.

recommendations.action: Bind payment destination to vendor-of-record data instead of quote-provided bank details, and require payments-agent to reject mismatches.
Require per-payment approval on the final vendor identity and payment destination, not only on the initial purchase request.

findings.title: Unpinned and unverified A2A peer definition enables spoofing or rug-pull of payments-agent

attack_path.note: Orchestrator consumes remote agent card at startup.
Delegated irreversible payment depends on the consumed peer definition and identity.

threat_refs.name: AI Supply Chain Compromise: AI Agent Tool

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor reaches moderate because the prompt vendor-list rule technically covers the delegated payment capability, but that behavioral rule does not address peer identity or definition integrity at all. The unexpressed design fact is that a spoofed or rug-pulled peer can change the meaning of the delegated sink without interacting with that prompt rule, so residual remains high.

forecast.watch_signal: Any change in agent card URL, peer endpoint, authentication mode, or addition of new peer agents should trigger reassessment because there are no present pinning or identity controls.

evidence.observation: The orchestrator relies on a fetched agent card advertising pay_vendor over bearer authentication.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token.

recommendations.action: Pin the agent card and verify peer identity with signed metadata or mutual identity controls before accepting task execution semantics.

findings.title: Missing attributable payment-action provenance across orchestrator to peer delegation
findings.residual_rationale: The floor computes to moderate because the prompt vendor-list rule is counted as a behavioral control touching the delegated payment capability, but prompt text cannot restore repudiation properties or create immutable cross-agent provenance. The design fact outside the control classification is that no cryptographic or record-bound link exists from manager approval to the peer's executed payment, so residual stays high.

forecast.watch_signal: Delegation to more peers or reduced review context will further weaken action attribution unless approval and payment records are cryptographically linked.

evidence.observation: The manager approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
The design assumes the peer will handle remaining checks, but no attributable linkage from approval to executed payment is described.

recommendations.action: Attach immutable approval identifiers and decision provenance to delegated payment tasks and record the peer's executed payment against that identifier.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts do not describe inbound agent authentication to the orchestrator process itself beyond the purchase request channel.
This design does not expose a separate confidential data egress from the orchestrator other than delegated payment instructions already covered elsewhere.
No spend loop, recursive delegation, or unbounded runtime is described for this orchestrator in the provided design artifacts.
The assessment concerns harmful influence from external vendor content, not attribution controls for the external sender.
The purchase request channel is explicitly SSO authenticated, so requester spoofing is not evidenced as a design weakness here.
The artifacts describe an authenticated request source and do not show a dispute over requester attribution in this design.
The inbound quote flow brings data in from outside; the present concern is malicious influence, not outbound disclosure on this flow.
No volume-driven service exhaustion or parser abuse path is described for inbound vendor quote email handling.
The described harm on this boundary-crossing flow is payment execution and authority misuse, not confidential data disclosure.
The artifacts do not indicate repeated or recursive delegation that would make this A2A flow a service exhaustion path.
The artifacts say the agent can read the approved vendor list, but they do not say who can modify it or how integrity is protected.
The approved vendor list is internal reference data, and no cross-tenant or external disclosure path from the store is described.
No availability dependency or lockout condition on the vendor list store is described in the supplied artifacts.
The design says an approval record exists, but not how it is protected from modification after approval.
The record contains approval context, but the evidenced risk is missing propagation and attribution rather than disclosure of the record itself.
No availability risk or dependency failure for the approval record store is documented in the provided case.
The peer agent is described as executing payments, not exposing confidential procurement data outside the boundary.
The case does not describe recursive tasks, spend loops, or operational saturation of the peer payment process.

rating.rationale: Highest present inherent risk is F2: untrusted vendor quote content can influence an irreversible delegated payment path, yielding critical inherent risk under the U-to-S3 matrix. Residual remains high because the only credited preventive control on that path is a behavioral prompt rule, worth one tier at rubric step 4. The manager approval does not qualify as a sink gate because it is not wired through approval_gate_ref and does not review final payment details. Forecast rises to critical when the prompt rule decays under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, longer_task_horizon, or intended_purpose_change. Manual validation performed against the provided schema and validation checklist; no runtime observation was available.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt, agent card, and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, A2A protocol traces, or payments-agent implementation details were provided, so controls inside the peer agent were assessed only from the consumed agent card and runtime notes.

No explicit logging, audit, or destination-binding configuration was provided, so provenance and recipient validation findings are based on stated design gaps rather than verified deployment settings.
Because no validator scripts could be run in this environment, schema and rubric checks were applied manually using the provided validation checklist.
